request.intent: Ask one question, with optional Context, and get one answer from an installed local Ollama model. Reuse this as an inexpensive private judgment step in future meta-workflows.

example.input: Question: Why did the backup fail? Context: disk free 0 GB; log says no space left on device. Reply as JSON with summary, cause and next_step.
example.expected_result: One answer string containing a JSON object; Check reply verifies the three text fields before Notify me queues a message.

request.target_device: AOTN TUI and headless authoring/run CLI on the owner machine; Telegram only in the example downstream workflow.
request.destination: Answer downstream and optionally in the Vault; Run details optionally in a separate Vault key.
request.trigger: One explicit node visit per question; no background scheduling, chat history or tools.
inputs: Required Question: Configured, Upstream payload or Vault text.
Optional Context: Not used (default), Configured, Upstream payload or Vault text.
Options-owned server URL and default installed model; optional per-node model override.
constraints: Owner approved decisions/samples 1–10; per-node tuning remains visible.
Build one PR; fake-server tests; exactly two real requests for one short JSON/thinking-off smoke scenario.
No merge, live workflow/configuration changes, pulls, retries or cloud fallback.
success: One Question plus optional Context produces one final local answer.
JSON mode returns text that Check reply can parse and validate.
Question and Context expose exactly their accepted source kinds; compatible upstream secondary Vault outputs are selectable.
Settings, per-node controls, output routing, bounded failures and headless authoring match the approved contract.
unknowns: Broader prompt quality, long-context token fit and device go-live remain unproven.

Headless nodes/describe/build/run expose the same contract as the TUI.
Generation and implementation require new owner authorization; no live sends in planning.

Public fixture uses an owner-configured model description; the exact private model identifier is in the local smoke receipt.
